title: Appendix C - External instruments and resources B1

blocks.text: Appendix C - External instruments and resources B1

These resources support the course; They don't replace him. Added to Appendix C of Volumes 2 and 3 (grammar, dictionaries, Aswaat Arabiyya, Kallimni ʿArabi Bishweesh, CIMA), which remain valid. Each tab indicates recipients, level, advantages, limits, cost and way of use. The information has been checked on the pages indicated as source on 24 October 2026. Prices, editions, schedules and availability change: check them again before buying or signing up. When a data was not indicated in a reliable source, the card says so. How to choose. In B1 four things are needed: a root dictionary (now indispensable), a source of graduated news, a source of authentic news to read and listen to every day, and authentic Egyptian material for the EGY track. The rest is optional.
C1 · Dictionaries

Hans Wehr, A Dictionary of Modern Written Arabic and Baldissera, The Arabic Dictionary (Volume 3, Appendix C1). In B1 the root dictionary becomes the daily tool: B1-01 explains the use, and in the tests and exams it is allowed in the translation test only. Check in the introduction of your bilingual dictionary if entries are sorted by root or alphabetical order.
C2 · Manual in English

Communicate in Arabic · Levels B1-B2 of the Common European Framework for Languages Monica Ruocco, Maria Avino, Caterina Pinto, Fares Aljaramneh · Hoepli, Necklace Oriental Studies (volume 3 of the course), April 2024 · ISBN 9788836011155 (paper), 9788836011162 (digital).
• Recipients: Italophones who have completed a journey A2-B1 of standard Arabic.
• Level: B1-B2; third volume of the series of which Volume 3 of this course recommended the second (A2-B1).
• Advantages: ten thematic units (environment and sustainability, health and well-being, work, migrants and refugees;

media, politics, parties and leisure, tourism, the digital world, halal economy and new energies); texts of different genres with understanding and analysis, vocabulary, grammar with exercises; in each unit an oral production section and a guided writing section; cultural notes and dialects; audio with interviews and podcasts; Arab-Italian glossary; XII-308 pages.
• Limits: arrives at B2, then in B1 the first part of it is mainly used; additional materials require the
publisher platform and a code.
• Cost: € 32,90 paper; € 26,99 Digital (Publisher's Price).
• Use during the course: second source of texts and listening in modules B1.3 and B1.4 and in B1-24; the themes of:
• Source: hoeplieditore.it
C3 · Gradual news and authentic news
Al Jazeera Learning Arabic ·
• Recipients: students of Arabic as a foreign language; the institute presents it mainly for journalists.
• Level: the same news is proposed at several levels; The page doesn't say how many.
• Advantages: the content of the news remains the same, while changing text length, complexity of
structures and speed of audio, from slow and clear to the natural rhythm of a news show; translation of the new vocabulary into English, French, Spanish and Turkish; new content every week.
• Limits: no English translation; the selection of news is that of the editorial staff.
• Cost: the presentation page does not indicate costs.
• Use during the course: from B1-15, one news per week at the highest level that you can follow; in recovery after
the exam, a simplified newsletter per day (Part IV, recovery path).
• Source: institution.aljazeera.net (page    •"Learn Arabic" Program Launches "News in Levels" Initiative)
Monte Carlo Doualiya ( ⁧مونت كارلو الدولية⁩ ) French public radio in Arabic, of the group France Médias Monde · mc-doualiya.com.
• Recipients: who wants authentic news in standard Arabic.
• Level: B1 high and above; The news is at natural speed.
• Advantages: transmit 24 hours on 24 towards the Middle East and the Maghreb, including by satellite and on the site;
information, insights and sports.
• Limits: real speed; part of the entertainment programs uses the dialect; the source consulted does not describe
The news schedule.
• Cost: free listening.
• Use during the course: for the level 3Of B1-18 (Authentic news): listen to a short news in the evening, after having
read the headlines of the day on a news site.
• Source: "Monte Carlo Doualiya" (en.wikipedia.org), which refers to the official website.

BBC News Arabic. Attention: the BBC Arabic radio closed in January 2023, after 85 years; The news site and the television channel remain. So do not look for his radio news, which some older manuals still quote. Source: Arabic BBC entry (en.wikipedia.org) and January articles 2023 on the closure. UN News in Arabic ( ⁧أخبار الأمم المتحدة⁩ ) · news.un.org/ar. The United Nations news service has an Arabic editorial staff. It is useful in INT-02 for the vocabulary of international organisations ( ⁧أَمِينٌ عَامٌّ⁩ · ⁧مَبْعُوثٌ خَاصٌّ⁩ · ⁧مَجْلِسُ الأَمْنِ⁩ ) and to read institutional news in a clear and standard Arabic. The pages you see do not say if the news also has an audio version. Source: un.org/ar (I refer to news in Arabic) and news.un.org (Arabic editorial).
C4 Institutional sources (INT-02)

For the form of an institution (INT-02, year 11) always use the official website of the institution or government: copy the Arabic name exactly as it is written, write down the link and date of consultation, and use the consolidated translation if the site has one. An example: Hayʾa ʿāmma li-l-istiʿlāmāt ( ⁧الهيئة العامة للاستعلامات⁩ , State Information Service) Egyptian, sis.gov.eg, which publishes in Arabic, English, French, Spanish and Chinese (source: Parlmany, 25 September 2025). Remember the rules of the INT track: only public sources, language method, no data on private citizens.
C5 · Check the news (INT-01)

Verification Handbook in Arabic. The European Journalism Centre's online news and content review manual has an Arabic edition, presented in 2016 from the Al Jazeera Training Centre (AJMTC) in collaboration with the European Journalism Centre. The website verificationhandbook.com hosts the manual; the page consulted does not confirm which links to the Arabic edition. It is a text for journalists: in INT-01 serves as a reading of the method (sources, images, testimonies) and as a source of vocabulary, always applied to public and uncontroversial themes. Source: network.aljazeera.net (-AJMTC Issues News Verification Handbook in Arabic)
C6 · Egyptian
Kallimni ʿArabi · An Intermediate Course in Spoken Egyptian Arabic 2 Samia Louis · The American University in Cairo Press, February 2011 · ISBN 9789774249778.
• Targets: those who already have the basis of Egyptian (about 30 hours of dialect; or 40 of standard Arabic, second
the publisher) and can read and write Arabic.
• Level: intermediate; follows Kallimni ʿArabi Bishweesh (Volume 3, Appendix C5).
• Advantages: ten lessons on practical situations (indications, purchases, projects, hobbies and leisure), second
ACTFL guidelines, with a prevalence of listening and speaking; audio of dialogues and exercises recorded by Egyptian speakers; 432 pages.
• Limits: in English; The editor's page doesn't say if it uses Arabic writing, transliteration or both.
• Cost: GBP 29,99 · USD 35,00 · EGP 700 (Publisher's prices).
• Use during the course: next to EGY-06 EGY-10 to have more dialogues and more listening; after B1, as
continuation of the track.
Source: aucpress.com

Egyptian series and films (EGY-10). For authentic listening they serve Egyptian series or films with Arabic subtitles. Platforms often change catalog and subtitle languages: before signing you up, check on a proof title that Arabic subtitles are there. An example is WATCH IT , Egyptian platform of video on demand subscription, dedicated to series, films, programs and Egyptian archive (source: elcinema.com, platform card); the form consulted does not indicate which titles have subtitles. Classic black and white films, slower and clearer, are often found on international platforms and on television: for them too, it controls subtitles title by title.
C7 · External certification
CIMA · Certificat international de maîtrise en arabe Institut du monde arabe (IMA), Paris. Updating the Volume tab 3.
• Targets: those who want an external and independent feedback of their standard Arabic level.
• Level: six levels CEFR, from A1 a C2.
• Tests: oral understanding (44 multiple choice questions, 60 minutes); written understanding (44 questions,
60 minutes); written production (three tasks, 60 minutes); recorded individual oral production (three tasks maximum) 11 minutes). In all less than three hours, with a break of 15 minutes.
• Advantages: more than fifty approved centres in almost twenty countries; valid certificate 3 years; can be repeated, with
at least 60 days between two sessions; The productions are corrected by two evaluators, with one third in case of strong divergence.
• Limits: the guide does not publish the percentage thresholds of the levels or the way in which the four skills are combined; i
reading texts are not vocized; dates and locations depend on the centers.
• Cost: determined by the examination centre; the guide does not indicate any amounts.
• Use during the course: after examination B1 of this course is the second time recommended for an external feedback.
The exam B1 of the course is not equivalent to CIMA: prepared with readings without vowels and listening at natural speed (C3).
• Source: CIMA candidate guide, version 5.2 updated to 15 June 2023, published on imarabe.org (file
of 2024, still the version available at the date of check).
C8 · Voice synthesis for scripts

As in previous volumes, the catalogue does not indicate a specific app. For scripts in fuṣḥā use an Arabic voice and compare the result with the tutor; in the news, vocal synthesis helps to fix the rhythm, but does not replace listening to real news (C3). For the Egyptian scripts of EGY units, vocal synthesis is not suitable: an Egyptian speaker is needed.
